title: Maximal slicing of a Cohen-Macaulay groupoid scheme at a finite type point, keeping h, s' and t' Cohen-Macaulay and locally of finite presentation

statement_spans.label: author lemma environment with its own label lemma-max-slice (no canonical tag in the snapshot tag list); statement at source lines 2245-2266

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: Since s is locally of finite presentation the fibre F_u is locally of finite type over kappa(u), so dim_{e(u)}(F_u) is finite and the proof argues by induction on it. If dim_{e(u)}(F_u) equals dim(G_u) there is nothing to prove. Otherwise the slice lemma applies and produces an immersion g : U' to U with properties (1), (2), (3), a strict dimension drop dim_{e(u)}(F'_u) < dim_{e(u)}(F_u) in place of (6), and h = s composed with pr_1 Cohen-Macaulay only at the point (u, e(u)) in place of (4) and (5). The local source remark yields the largest open U'' of U' on which h is Cohen-Macaulay, which contains (u, e(u)) and hence u, and after replacing U' by U'' the morphism h is Cohen-Macaulay everywhere; the restrict-property lemma, together with base change of locally finite presentation morphisms and base change of Cohen-Macaulay morphisms, then shows s' and t' are locally of finite presentation and Cohen-Macaulay. The dimension has dropped, so the induction hypothesis applies to the restricted groupoid at the point u, which is still a finite type point of U' by the identification of finite type points. The solution g' : U'' to U' of the restricted problem composes with g to a map g'' = g composed with g' which solves the original problem: properties (1), (2), (3), (5) and (6) are immediate, and (4) holds because h'' is locally of finite presentation and Cohen-Macaulay by the double restrict-property lemma, using that Cohen-Macaulay morphisms are fppf local on the target. (source lines 2268-2323)

core_obligations: Set up the induction: s locally of finite presentation makes F_u locally of finite type over kappa(u), so dim_{e(u)}(F_u) is finite, and one argues by induction on this dimension (proof lines 2269-2272). Base case: if dim_{e(u)}(F_u) = dim(G_u) there is nothing to prove (proof line 2275). Induction step: if the dimension is strictly larger, lemma-slice applies and yields g : U' to U with properties (1), (2), (3), a strict drop dim_{e(u)}(F'_u) < dim_{e(u)}(F_u) instead of (6), and h = s composed with pr_1 Cohen-Macaulay at the point (u, e(u)) instead of (4) and (5) (proof lines 2276-2285). Apply remark-local-source-apply to obtain the largest open U'' of U' on which h is Cohen-Macaulay; since (u, e(u)) lies in it, u lies in U'', and after replacing U' by U'' the morphism h is Cohen-Macaulay everywhere; then lemma-restrict-property with the base change lemmas morphisms-lemma-base-change-finite-presentation and more-morphisms-lemma-base-change-CM shows s' and t' are locally of finite presentation and Cohen-Macaulay (proof lines 2285-2298). The dimension drop lets the induction hypothesis apply to (U', R', s', t', c') at u, which is a finite type point of U' by morphisms-lemma-identify-finite-type-points (proof lines 2300-2306). Let g' : U'' to U' with (U'', R'', s'', t'', c'') solve the restricted problem; the composition g'' = g composed with g' solves the original problem: properties (1), (2), (3), (5), (6) are immediate from the two solutions, and (4) holds because h'' is locally of finite presentation and Cohen-Macaulay by lemma-double-restrict-property, which uses more-morphisms-lemma-CM-local-source-and-target that Cohen-Macaulay morphisms are fppf local on the target (proof lines 2307-2322).
proof_roadmap: Set up induction on the finite dimension dim_{e(u)}(F_u) and treat the equal-dimension base case (proof lines 2269-2275).
Slice once with lemma-slice and shrink U' to the largest open where h is Cohen-Macaulay using remark-local-source-apply (proof lines 2276-2292).
Transfer local finite presentation and Cohen-Macaulayness to s' and t' via lemma-restrict-property and the two base change lemmas (proof lines 2293-2298).

Apply the induction hypothesis to the restricted groupoid and verify the composed map g'' = g composed with g' satisfies all six properties, (4) via lemma-double-restrict-property and fppf locality of Cohen-Macaulay (proof lines 2300-2322).
